description: Patch releases are deliberately not automerged here, unlike in most other roles in this fleet.

Open WebUI applies its Alembic migrations automatically at container start (run_migrations() in open_webui/config.py, unless ENABLE_DB_MIGRATIONS is turned off), forward-only, and its patch releases do ship them: 0.11.0 -> 0.11.1 added four, among them repair_double_encoded_user_oauth, which rewrites existing rows of the user table, and 0.12.0 -> 0.12.1 added add_missing_auth_rows and add_apps.

An automerged patch would therefore rewrite the schema of the database holding the users' accounts and chats, unattended and with no way back short of restoring a backup. The Molecule run does not cover this: it installs onto an empty database, so it never performs the step from the previous release's schema, which is the only migration an automerged bump would run in production.

packageRules.description: Only consider the plain `0.12.4` tags. ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui publishes every release under two tags, `0.12.4` and `v0.12.4`, which semver treats as one version, so Renovate would otherwise write whichever the registry listed last, and `v0.12.4` fails the Molecule assertion against the version the API reports, which never carries the `v`. The rule also leaves out the flavoured `-cuda`, `-ollama` and `-slim` tags, which strict semver already skips as prereleases, and the floating `0.12`, `main`, `dev` and `latest` tags, which are not versions.
